I read all 380 commits and the 127-row PR sheet. Here's the breakdown:

| Type | Count | User-facing? |
|---|---|---|
| chore (mostly deps) | 153 | No |
| refactor | 73 | Mostly no — **but 9 touch the public surface** |
| test | 64 | No |
| ci | 33 | No |
| fix | 26 | Yes → collapses to ~11 distinct |
| perf | 10 | Arguably |
| feat | 1 | Yes |

The 380 commits contain about **15 things a user would notice**. Much of the noise is literal duplication — `fix(api): keep the trace id across the retry` appears 3×, `fix(core): drop the duplicate header` 3×, the same pino bump lands 8 times.

## What actually changed

**Behavior changes people will hit**

- `fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403` (#4223) — this is the big one. It's labeled a fix, but any client branching on 403 breaks. I'd put it under Breaking, not Fixed.
- `refactor(*): stop re-exporting the internal error types` — 8 commits across auth, billing, core, db, jobs. "Refactor" undersells it: imports that used to resolve now won't.
- `refactor(api): drop the unused v1 export route` (#4152) — "unused" is the author's read of internal telemetry, not a guarantee. It's a removed HTTP route.

**The one feature**

- `feat(webhooks): retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff` (#4191). It also touched `src/core/config.js`, so it almost certainly ships a new config option — you'll want the option name and default in the note.

**Real fixes**, deduped across modules:

- HTTP client: timer no longer leaks when the socket drops; pool now closes on shutdown
- Paginator no longer throws on a null cursor (hit api, db, queue, webhooks — one symptom, four call sites)
- Duplicate header no longer sent (core, http, billing)
- Trace id survives a retry
- Empty allowlist no longer errors (db, jobs, store)
- Trailing slash trimmed once, not twice (jobs, queue)
- Latency histogram was reporting the wrong units (core, store) — worth calling out separately if anyone dashboards these
- `fix(db): stop logging the whole request body` (#4157) — logged request bodies may sit in existing log stores; that's arguably a note for operators, not just a bugfix line

## Draft for CHANGELOG.md

```markdown
## 4.2.0 — 2026-08-28

### Breaking
- An expired token now returns 401 instead of 403. If you branch on the
  status code, update that check.
- The internal error types are no longer re-exported from `auth`, `billing`,
  `core`, `db`, and `jobs`. Import them from their own module.
- The v1 export route has been removed.

### Added
- Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff.
  <!-- confirm the config option name + default from src/core/config.js -->

### Fixed
- The HTTP client no longer leaks a timer when the socket drops, and now
  closes its pool on shutdown.
- Paginating with a null cursor no longer throws.
- A retry keeps the trace id.
- An empty allowlist is handled instead of erroring.
- Requests no longer carry a duplicated header.
- The latency histogram reports the correct units.
- Request bodies are no longer written to the logs.
```

## Two things to check before you ship

**Node version.** Four `docs: note the minimum node version` commits and six `ci: run the suite on node 22` commits, but I see no `engines` change in any `package.json` diff — every `package.json` edit sits inside a dep-bump commit. If the floor really did move, that's a Breaking line and it's currently missing. If it didn't, the docs are ahead of the code.

**The PR sheet is not a complete record.** It lists 15 user-facing PRs; the commit log has 37. Both `fix(http)` items, `fix(api): guard the null cursor`, `fix(db): handle an empty allowlist`, and `fix(core): use the right units` exist only as commits. Don't build the notes from the sheet.

I left the 10 `perf` commits out to keep the three headings your template specifies — the two worth mentioning are `perf(api): reuse the parsed schema between requests` and `perf(core): skip the JSON round-trip on the hot path`. Say the word and I'll fold them in or write the draft into CHANGELOG.md.
